entries.name: ln
entries.description: Calculate the natural logarithm (base e) of a number. Returns ln(x) where e^ln(x) = x.
entries.reason: Natural log is transcendental/float; no place in an exact integer substrate.

entries.name: log
entries.description: Calculate the logarithm of a number to a specified base. Returns log_base(x).
entries.reason: Arbitrary-base float logarithm is transcendental.

entries.name: log10
entries.description: Calculate the base-10 (common) logarithm of a number. Returns log₁₀(x).
entries.reason: Base-10 float logarithm is transcendental.

entries.name: log2
entries.description: Calculate the base-2 (binary) logarithm of a number. Returns log₂(x).
entries.reason: Float log2 (not the integer floor-log2 that bit_length gives) is transcendental.

entries.name: exp
entries.description: Calculate e raised to the power of x. Returns e^x, the exponential function.
entries.reason: e^x is transcendental/float.

entries.name: ceiling_multiple
entries.description: Round a number up to the nearest multiple of significance. Always rounds away from zero.
entries.reason: Round a number up to the nearest multiple of a step is exactly snap_up.

entries.name: floor_multiple
entries.description: Round a number down to the nearest multiple of significance. Always rounds toward zero.
entries.reason: Round a number down to the nearest multiple of a step is exactly snap_down.

entries.name: mround
entries.description: Round a number to the nearest multiple of significance. Uses standard rounding rules.
entries.reason: Round to the nearest multiple (ties up) is exactly round_to_multiple.

entries.name: decimal_to_base
entries.description: Convert a decimal number to its representation in another base (2-36).
entries.reason: Arbitrary base 2-36 string output needs variable-length alphanumeric output beyond cell80's small fixed-field cell shape.

entries.name: base_to_decimal
entries.description: Convert a number from a specified base (2-36) to decimal.
entries.reason: Parsing an arbitrary-base string input is string processing outside the integer/fraction substrate.

entries.name: quotient
entries.description: Return the integer quotient of division without remainder. Equivalent to a // b.
entries.reason: Plain integer quotient (a // b) is exactly div_floor_u32 (or safe_div at u16 width).

entries.name: double_factorial
entries.description: Calculate double factorial n!! = n × (n-2) × (n-4) × ...
entries.reason: n!! (double factorial) is a genuinely new bounded recurrence, same checked-overflow shape as factorial_checked_u32; no existing cell computes it.

entries.name: multinomial
entries.description: Calculate the multinomial coefficient. Generalization of binomial coefficient for multiple groups.
entries.reason: Takes an unbounded List[int] of group sizes, not a fixed small arg count.

entries.name: sum_product
entries.description: Calculate the sum of products of corresponding elements in multiple arrays.
entries.reason: Takes nested List[List[Number]] arrays; unbounded, not scalar.

entries.name: sum_squares
entries.description: Calculate the sum of squares of numbers in a list.
entries.reason: Takes an unbounded List[Number], not a fixed small arg count.

entries.name: random_float
entries.description: Generate a random float between 0 and 1 (exclusive of 1).
entries.reason: Float RNG in [0,1) needs float representation.

entries.name: random_int
entries.description: Generate a random integer between min_val and max_val (inclusive).
entries.reason: Ranged random integer composes directly from the existing lcg_next generator plus safe_mod, the same range-mapping pattern epsilon_greedy_pick3 already uses.

entries.name: random_array
entries.description: Generate an array of random numbers with specified dimensions.
entries.reason: Generates a 2D List[List[float]] of unbounded/variable size.

entries.name: product
entries.description: Calculate the product of all numbers in a list. Returns the multiplication of all elements.
entries.reason: Takes an unbounded List[Number] to multiply, not a fixed small arg count.

entries.name: arabic_to_roman
entries.description: Convert an Arabic number to Roman numeral representation.
entries.reason: Roman-numeral string output is variable-length alphanumeric, outside cell80's small fixed-field cell shape.

entries.name: roman_to_arabic
entries.description: Convert a Roman numeral to Arabic number representation.
entries.reason: Parsing a Roman-numeral string input is string processing outside the integer substrate.

entries.name: series_sum
entries.description: Calculate the sum of an arithmetic series based on first term, last term, and number of terms.
entries.reason: Same closed-form sum as arithmetic_series_sum but parameterized by endpoints (first,last,count) instead of (a,d,n); composing via avg2-then-multiply is unsound (avg2 floors before the multiply, corrupting odd first+last cases), and deriving d then calling arithmetic_series_sum needs an extra exact-division step, so a dedicated endpoint-based cell is the safe, minimal implementation.

entries.name: minimum
entries.description: Find the smaller of two numbers.
entries.reason: Smaller of two values is exactly min.

entries.name: maximum
entries.description: Find the larger of two numbers.
entries.reason: Larger of two values is exactly max.

entries.name: clamp
entries.description: Clamp a value between a minimum and maximum bound. Ensures the value stays within specified limits.
entries.reason: Clamp to [min,max] is exactly clamp.

entries.name: sort_numbers
entries.description: Sort a list of numbers in ascending or descending order.
entries.reason: Returns an unbounded sorted List[Number].

entries.name: rank_numbers
entries.description: Get the rank (1-based position) of each number in a list when sorted. Handles ties appropriately.
entries.reason: Returns an unbounded List[int] of ranks.

entries.name: min_list
entries.description: Find the minimum value in a list of numbers.
entries.reason: Takes an unbounded List[Number]; min3/min only cover fixed small arities.

entries.name: max_list
entries.description: Find the maximum value in a list of numbers.
entries.reason: Takes an unbounded List[Number]; max3/max only cover fixed small arities.

entries.name: equal
entries.description: Check if two numbers are exactly equal. For floating-point numbers, consider using approximately_equal instead.
entries.reason: a == b is exactly eq.

entries.name: not_equal
entries.description: Check if two numbers are not equal.
entries.reason: a != b is exactly neq.

entries.name: less_than
entries.description: Check if the first number is less than the second number.
entries.reason: a < b is exactly is_lt.

entries.name: less_than_or_equal
entries.description: Check if the first number is less than or equal to the second number.
entries.reason: a <= b is exactly is_le.

entries.name: greater_than
entries.description: Check if the first number is greater than the second number.
entries.reason: a > b is exactly is_gt.

entries.name: greater_than_or_equal
entries.description: Check if the first number is greater than or equal to the second number.
entries.reason: a >= b is exactly is_ge.

entries.name: in_range
entries.description: Check if a number is within a specified range (inclusive by default).
entries.reason: Dynamic-inclusive range test is a straight dispatch between the two existing bound predicates cell80 already ships.

entries.name: between
entries.description: Check if a value is between two bounds (exclusive by default, like mathematical interval notation).
entries.reason: Strict lo < x < hi is exactly between_exclusive.

entries.name: approximately_equal
entries.description: Check if two floating-point numbers are approximately equal within a tolerance. Handles floating-point precision issues.
entries.reason: Float tolerance comparison; needs float precision semantics.

entries.name: close_to_zero
entries.description: Check if a number is close to zero within a tolerance. Useful for floating-point comparisons.
entries.reason: Float near-zero tolerance check.

entries.name: is_finite
entries.description: Check if a number is finite (not infinite and not NaN).
entries.reason: Float finiteness has no meaning over cell80's plain unsigned integers.

entries.name: is_nan
entries.description: Check if a number is NaN (Not a Number).
entries.reason: NaN is an IEEE-754 float concept, not representable in the integer dialect.

entries.name: is_infinite
entries.description: Check if a number is infinite (positive or negative infinity).
entries.reason: Float infinity has no representation in the integer dialect.

entries.name: is_normal
entries.description: Check if a number is normal (finite, non-zero, and not subnormal).
entries.reason: Float normal/subnormal classification is IEEE-754-specific.

entries.name: is_close
entries.description: Relative tolerance comparison using both absolute and relative tolerances.
entries.reason: Combined relative/absolute float tolerance comparison.

entries.name: add
entries.description: Add two numbers together. Pure arithmetic addition operation.
entries.reason: Basic addition is exactly add_sat (or add_checked_u32 for the escalating wide form).

entries.name: subtract
entries.description: Subtract the second number from the first number.
entries.reason: Basic subtraction is exactly sub_sat.

entries.name: multiply
entries.description: Multiply two numbers together.
entries.reason: Basic multiplication is exactly mul_sat.

entries.name: divide
entries.description: Divide the first number by the second number.
entries.reason: Basic integer division with a divide-by-zero guard is exactly safe_div (or q_div for the fixed-point fractional form); a literal float quotient isn't representable anyway.

entries.name: power
entries.description: Raise a number to a power. Handles integer and fractional exponents.
entries.reason: Explicitly supports fractional exponents (e.g. x^0.5), needing transcendental/float pow beyond pow_checked_u32's integer-only exponent.

entries.name: sqrt
entries.description: Calculate the square root of a number.
entries.reason: Float square root of an arbitrary number is generally irrational; isqrt only covers the integer floor-root case.

entries.name: abs_value
entries.description: Calculate the absolute value of a number.
entries.reason: Absolute value of a signed value is exactly abs_i16.

entries.name: sign
entries.description: Determine the sign of a number. Returns 1, -1, or 0.
entries.reason: Sign (+1/-1/0) of a signed value is exactly sign_i16.

entries.name: negate
entries.description: Negate a number (return its additive inverse).
entries.reason: No existing cell negates a signed i16 value; like abs_i16, it would need to special-case i16::MIN (which can't be negated in-range) -- small but genuinely missing.

entries.name: modulo
entries.description: Calculate the modulo (remainder) of division. Returns a % b.
entries.reason: a % b with a divide-by-zero guard is exactly safe_mod.

entries.name: divmod_operation
entries.description: Perform division and return both quotient and remainder. Returns (quotient, remainder).
entries.reason: Quotient-and-remainder pair is a direct pairing of two existing division cells.

entries.name: mod_power
entries.description: Calculate modular exponentiation: (base^exponent) mod modulus. Efficient for large numbers.
entries.reason: Modular exponentiation (base^exp mod modulus) is exactly pow_mod_u32 (or pow_mod at u16 width).

entries.name: remainder
entries.description: Calculate floating-point remainder of division (IEEE remainder operation).
entries.reason: IEEE-754 float remainder operation, distinct from integer modulo.

entries.name: fmod
entries.description: Calculate floating-point modulo operation. Similar to % but for floats.
entries.reason: Floating-point modulo operation.

entries.name: round_number
entries.description: Round a number to a specified number of decimal places.
entries.reason: Rounding to N decimal places is inherently a float/decimal operation; meaningless on cell80's plain integers.

entries.name: floor
entries.description: Return the floor of a number (largest integer less than or equal to x).
entries.reason: Floor of a generic Number targets float/fractional inputs; a no-op on plain integers.

entries.name: ceil
entries.description: Return the ceiling of a number (smallest integer greater than or equal to x).
entries.reason: Ceiling of a generic Number targets float/fractional inputs; a no-op on plain integers.

entries.name: truncate
entries.description: Truncate a number towards zero (remove decimal part).
entries.reason: Truncation toward zero targets float/fractional inputs; a no-op on plain integers.

entries.name: pi
entries.description: Get the mathematical constant π (pi) ≈ 3.14159. The ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant.

entries.name: e
entries.description: Get Euler's number e ≈ 2.71828. Base of natural logarithm and fundamental constant in calculus.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant.

entries.name: tau
entries.description: Get tau (τ) ≈ 6.28318. Equal to 2π, represents a full turn in radians.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant (2*pi).

entries.name: infinity
entries.description: Get positive infinity. Represents unbounded growth or division by zero limit.
entries.reason: IEEE-754 float special value, not representable in the integer dialect.

entries.name: nan
entries.description: Get NaN (Not a Number). Represents undefined or invalid mathematical operations.
entries.reason: IEEE-754 float special value, not representable in the integer dialect.

entries.name: golden_ratio
entries.description: Get the golden ratio φ ≈ 1.61803. Appears in art, nature, and Fibonacci sequence.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant.

entries.name: silver_ratio
entries.description: Get the silver ratio δ ≈ 2.41421. Equal to 1 + √2, appears in octagon constructions.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant.

entries.name: plastic_number
entries.description: Get the plastic number ρ ≈ 1.32472. Real root of x³ = x + 1, related to Padovan sequence.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant (real root of x^3=x+1).

entries.name: sqrt2
entries.description: Get √2 ≈ 1.41421. Square root of 2, first known irrational number.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant.

entries.name: sqrt3
entries.description: Get √3 ≈ 1.73205. Square root of 3, appears in equilateral triangles.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant.

entries.name: sqrt5
entries.description: Get √5 ≈ 2.23607. Square root of 5, appears in golden ratio formula.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant.

entries.name: cbrt2
entries.description: Get ∛2 ≈ 1.25992. Cube root of 2, edge length of cube with volume 2.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant.

entries.name: cbrt3
entries.description: Get ∛3 ≈ 1.44225. Cube root of 3, edge length of cube with volume 3.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant.

entries.name: ln2
entries.description: Get ln(2) ≈ 0.69315. Natural logarithm of 2, appears in information theory.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant (transcendental log).

entries.name: ln10
entries.description: Get ln(10) ≈ 2.30259. Natural logarithm of 10, conversion factor for logarithms.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant (transcendental log).

entries.name: log2e
entries.description: Get log₂(e) ≈ 1.44270. Logarithm base 2 of e, conversion factor for binary logarithms.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant.

entries.name: log10e
entries.description: Get log₁₀(e) ≈ 0.43429. Common logarithm of e, conversion factor for base 10 logarithms.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant.

entries.name: euler_gamma
entries.description: Get the Euler-Mascheroni constant γ ≈ 0.57722. Limit of harmonic series minus natural logarithm.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant (Euler-Mascheroni).

entries.name: catalan
entries.description: Get Catalan's constant G ≈ 0.91597. Sum of alternating series 1 - 1/9 + 1/25 - 1/49 + ...
entries.reason: Catalan's constant is an irrational float series sum, distinct from cell80's existing catalan_number (integer Catalan-number sequence).

entries.name: apery
entries.description: Get Apéry's constant ζ(3) ≈ 1.20206. Sum of cubes reciprocals: 1 + 1/8 + 1/27 + ...
entries.reason: Irrational float constant (zeta(3)).

entries.name: khinchin
entries.description: Get Khinchin's constant K ≈ 2.68545. Geometric mean of continued fraction coefficients.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant.

entries.name: glaisher
entries.description: Get the Glaisher-Kinkelin constant A ≈ 1.28243. Related to Barnes G-function and hyperfactorials.
entries.reason: Irrational float constant.

entries.name: machine_epsilon
entries.description: Get machine epsilon for floating-point precision. Smallest value where 1 + ε > 1.
entries.reason: Float-precision concept, meaningless for exact integers.

entries.name: max_float
entries.description: Get the maximum finite floating-point value. Largest representable float.
entries.reason: Float representable-range constant.

entries.name: min_float
entries.description: Get the minimum positive normalized floating-point value. Smallest positive normal float.
entries.reason: Float representable-range constant.

entries.name: miller_rabin_test
entries.description: Miller-Rabin probabilistic primality test. Industry standard for cryptographic applications.
entries.reason: Probabilistic primality testing exists to scale past exact trial division into arbitrary-precision/cryptographic ranges; at u32 scale is_prime_u32 already gives an exact deterministic answer.

entries.name: solovay_strassen_test
entries.description: Solovay-Strassen probabilistic primality test using Jacobi symbols.
entries.reason: Same rationale as miller_rabin_test: only useful beyond u32/bignum scale, where is_prime_u32's exact trial division already suffices.

entries.name: fermat_primality_test
entries.description: Fermat primality test. Simple but can be fooled by Carmichael numbers.
entries.reason: Probabilistic test whose value is at arbitrary-precision scale beyond is_prime_u32's exact u32 coverage.

entries.name: aks_primality_test
entries.description: AKS primality test - first deterministic polynomial-time algorithm.
entries.reason: Polynomial-time-but-expensive deterministic test aimed at arbitrary-precision numbers; far outside a tiny fixed-cost cell's budget.

entries.name: deterministic_miller_rabin
entries.description: Deterministic Miller-Rabin test using known witnesses for specific ranges.
entries.reason: Fixed-witness deterministic variant targets numbers well beyond u32, where is_prime_u32 already suffices exactly.

entries.name: strong_pseudoprime_test
entries.description: Test if a number is a strong pseudoprime to given bases.
entries.reason: Takes an unbounded List[int] of bases and targets the same beyond-u32 primality niche as the other advanced_primality functions.

entries.name: carmichael_number_test
entries.description: Test if a number is a Carmichael number (pseudoprime to all bases).
entries.reason: Korselt's criterion (n square-free and (p-1)|(n-1) for every prime factor p) is a bounded, deterministic integer test buildable from a smallest_prime_factor-style factorization loop; genuinely new.

entries.name: cousin_primes
entries.description: Find cousin prime pairs (p, p+4) up to limit.
entries.reason: Returns an unbounded List[List[int]] of all pairs up to limit, like 'list all primes up to n'.

entries.name: sexy_primes
entries.description: Find sexy prime pairs (p, p+6) up to limit.
entries.reason: Returns an unbounded List[List[int]] of all pairs up to limit.

entries.name: prime_triplets
entries.description: Find all prime triplets up to limit.
entries.reason: Returns an unbounded List[Dict] of all triplets up to limit.

entries.name: prime_quadruplets
entries.description: Find all prime quadruplets up to limit.
entries.reason: Returns an unbounded List[Dict] of all quadruplets up to limit.

entries.name: prime_constellations
entries.description: Find prime constellations of specified pattern.
entries.reason: Takes a List[int] pattern and returns an unbounded List[List[int]] of matches up to limit.

entries.name: is_admissible_pattern
entries.description: Check if a given pattern is admissible for prime constellations.
entries.reason: Takes an unbounded List[int] pattern argument, not a fixed small arg count.

entries.name: prime_counting_function
entries.description: Approximate the prime counting function π(x).
entries.reason: Returns an approximation (float/log-based) of pi(x); exact counting up to large x is also unbounded work.

entries.name: prime_number_theorem_error
entries.description: Analyze the error in Prime Number Theorem approximation.
entries.reason: Analyzes float/log-based approximation error against pi(x).

entries.name: prime_gaps_analysis
entries.description: Analyze prime gaps in a given range.
entries.reason: Scans an arbitrary [start,end] range and returns an unbounded Dict of gap data.

entries.name: bertrand_postulate_verify
entries.description: Verify Bertrand's postulate for given n.
entries.reason: Requires searching for a witness prime across a range up to 2n, which can blow past a tiny fixed cycle budget for large n (the same concern is_prime_u32 already documents).

entries.name: twin_prime_conjecture_data
entries.description: Collect data about twin prime conjecture up to limit.
entries.reason: Returns an unbounded Dict/list of twin-prime pairs up to limit.

entries.name: prime_gap_records
entries.description: Find record prime gaps (first occurrence of each gap size).
entries.reason: Returns an unbounded List of record gaps up to limit.

entries.name: prime_density_analysis
entries.description: Analyze prime density in intervals.
entries.reason: Scans and returns an unbounded Dict of density data over intervals.

entries.name: ulam_spiral_analysis
entries.description: Generate data for Ulam spiral prime visualization.
entries.reason: Generates an unbounded 2D grid of visualization data.

entries.name: euler_totient
entries.description: Calculate Euler's totient function φ(n) - count of integers ≤ n coprime to n.
entries.reason: Identical function and definition to cell80's existing euler_totient.

entries.name: jordan_totient
entries.description: Calculate Jordan's totient function J_k(n) - generalization of Euler's totient.
entries.reason: Jordan's totient J_k(n) generalizes euler_totient with an exponent parameter k; genuinely new, bounded, small arg count (n,k).

entries.name: mobius_function
entries.description: Calculate the Möbius function μ(n).
entries.reason: Mobius function mu(n) is a classic bounded number-theoretic function (via square-free/prime-factor-count check); not present in cell80.

entries.name: little_omega
entries.description: Calculate ω(n) - number of distinct prime factors.
entries.reason: omega(n), count of distinct prime factors, is a bounded trial-division loop distinct from factor_count (which counts divisors, not distinct primes); genuinely new.

entries.name: big_omega
entries.description: Calculate Ω(n) - total number of prime factors (with multiplicity).
entries.reason: Omega(n), total prime factors with multiplicity, is a bounded trial-division loop; genuinely new and distinct from little_omega/factor_count.

entries.name: divisor_power_sum
entries.description: Calculate σ_k(n) - sum of kth powers of divisors.
entries.reason: sigma_k(n) generalizes both factor_count (k=0) and sum_divisors (k=1) with an exponent parameter -- the same 'missing general-parameter sibling' shape cell80 already uses elsewhere (e.g. weighted_sum2 generalizing weighted_sum).

entries.name: von_mangoldt_function
entries.description: Calculate the von Mangoldt function Λ(n).
entries.reason: Returns ln(p) for prime powers, a transcendental float value.

entries.name: liouville_function
entries.description: Calculate the Liouville function λ(n) = (-1)^Ω(n).
entries.reason: lambda(n) = (-1)^Omega(n) is a bounded sign-parity function over prime-factor count; no existing cell computes it (big_omega itself doesn't exist yet either, so it isn't reachable via composition).

entries.name: carmichael_lambda
entries.description: Calculate the Carmichael function λ(n) - exponent of multiplicative group mod n.
entries.reason: The Carmichael function needs full prime-power factorization plus an lcm combination step; bounded and deterministic (same complexity class as crt_solve_pair/mod_inverse's multi-step number theory) but a second-tier, more involved candidate.

entries.name: is_perfect_number
entries.description: Check if a number is perfect (equals sum of its proper divisors).
entries.reason: Perfect-number check is a direct comparison against the existing sum_divisors cell (sigma(n) == 2n).

entries.name: is_abundant_number
entries.description: Check if a number is abundant (sum of proper divisors > n).
entries.reason: Abundant-number check composes directly from sum_divisors plus a wide greater-than compare.

entries.name: is_deficient_number
entries.description: Check if a number is deficient (sum of proper divisors < n).
entries.reason: Deficient-number check composes directly from sum_divisors plus a wide less-than compare.

entries.name: perfect_numbers_up_to
entries.description: Find all perfect numbers up to limit using Euclid-Euler theorem.
entries.reason: Returns an unbounded List[int] of all perfect numbers up to limit.

entries.name: is_perfect_square
entries.description: Check if a number is a perfect square.
entries.reason: Perfect-square check is exactly is_square.

entries.name: perfect_squares
entries.description: Generate the first n perfect squares.
entries.reason: Returns an unbounded List[int] of the first n squares.

entries.name: nth_perfect_square
entries.description: Get the nth perfect square (0-indexed).
entries.reason: The nth (0-indexed) perfect square is exactly n*n, i.e. square_wide(n).

entries.name: is_power_of_two
entries.description: Check if a number is a power of two.
entries.reason: Power-of-two check is exactly is_pow2.

entries.name: powers_of_two
entries.description: Generate the first n powers of two.
entries.reason: Returns an unbounded List[int] of the first n powers of two.

entries.name: nth_power_of_two
entries.description: Get the nth power of two (0-indexed).
entries.reason: 2^n composes directly from the existing checked-power cell with base fixed at 2.

entries.name: fibonacci
entries.description: Calculate the nth Fibonacci number using efficient matrix exponentiation.
entries.reason: The nth Fibonacci number is exactly fibonacci_checked_u32.

entries.name: fibonacci_sequence
entries.description: Generate the first n Fibonacci numbers.
entries.reason: Returns an unbounded List[int] of the first n Fibonacci numbers.

entries.name: is_fibonacci_number
entries.description: Check if a number is a Fibonacci number.
entries.reason: Testing whether n is a Fibonacci number (via the classic 5n^2 +/- 4 perfect-square test) is bounded and deterministic, but 5n^2 overflows u16 fast, so it needs its own wide-checked cell rather than a trivial is_square composition.

entries.name: factorial
entries.description: Calculate factorial n! = n × (n-1) × ... × 2 × 1.
entries.reason: n! is exactly factorial_checked_u32.

entries.name: subfactorial
entries.description: Calculate subfactorial !n (derangements of n items).
entries.reason: Subfactorial !n (derangements of n items) is exactly derangement_count.

entries.name: triangular_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth triangular number T_n = n(n+1)/2.
entries.reason: T_n = n(n+1)/2 is exactly triangular.

entries.name: is_triangular_number
entries.description: Check if a number is a triangular number.
entries.reason: Whether x is triangular is exactly the success/escalate outcome of triangular_inverse_exact.

entries.name: triangular_sequence
entries.description: Generate the first n triangular numbers.
entries.reason: Returns an unbounded List[int] of the first n triangular numbers.

entries.name: pentagonal_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth pentagonal number P_n = n(3n-1)/2.
entries.reason: P_n = n(3n-1)/2 is a genuinely new figurate-number formula, same shape as the existing triangular cell; no pentagonal cell exists.

entries.name: is_pentagonal_number
entries.description: Check if a number is a pentagonal number.
entries.reason: Inverse pentagonal-number test (via isqrt on 24x+1) mirrors triangular_inverse_exact's pattern; likely ships as one dual-purpose pentagonal_inverse_exact cell alongside pentagonal_number.

entries.name: pentagonal_sequence
entries.description: Generate the first n pentagonal numbers.
entries.reason: Returns an unbounded List[int] of the first n pentagonal numbers.

entries.name: square_pyramidal_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth square pyramidal number.
entries.reason: Sum of the first n squares, n(n+1)(2n+1)/6, is a genuinely new figurate/pyramidal-number formula parallel to triangular_number; no existing cell computes it.

entries.name: tetrahedral_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth tetrahedral number (sum of first n triangular numbers).
entries.reason: Tetrahedral(n) = C(n+2,3), a known binomial identity, trivially built from add_checked_u32 + choose_u32.

entries.name: catalan_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth Catalan number C_n = (2n)!/(n+1)!n!.
entries.reason: Exact match: cell80 already ships an nth-Catalan-number cell with the same recurrence and overflow-escalation behavior.

entries.name: catalan_sequence
entries.description: Generate the first n Catalan numbers.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length List[int] of the first n Catalan numbers, not a fixed-cost scalar/tuple output.

entries.name: is_catalan_number
entries.description: Check if a number is a Catalan number.
entries.reason: Genuine bounded predicate (iterate catalan_number until >= n, compare) not covered by any existing cell.

entries.name: bell_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth Bell number B_n (number of partitions of a set).
entries.reason: Distinct combinatorial sequence (set partitions) computable via a bounded triangle recurrence, not covered.

entries.name: bell_sequence
entries.description: Generate the first n Bell numbers.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length list of the first n Bell numbers.

entries.name: bell_triangle
entries.description: Generate Bell's triangle up to row n.
entries.reason: Returns a 2D list (List[List[int]]), far beyond a fixed-cost cell output.

entries.name: stirling_second
entries.description: Calculate Stirling number of the second kind S(n,k).
entries.reason: Two-arg bounded exact recurrence (subset partition counts), genuinely new and not composable from existing cells.

entries.name: stirling_first
entries.description: Calculate Stirling number of the first kind s(n,k) - FIXED IMPLEMENTATION.
entries.reason: Two-arg bounded exact recurrence, distinct from Stirling second kind, not covered.

entries.name: stirling_second_row
entries.description: Generate row n of Stirling numbers of the second kind.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length list (an entire row of Stirling numbers).

entries.name: narayana_number
entries.description: Calculate Narayana number N(n,k) = (1/n) * C(n,k) * C(n,k-1) - FIXED.
entries.reason: Niche combinatorial identity (N(n,k)=C(n,k)*C(n,k-1)/n) with low real-world value; mechanically reduces to existing choose_u32 arithmetic rather than needing its own cell.

entries.name: narayana_triangle_row
entries.description: Generate row n of Narayana triangle - FIXED.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length list (a full triangle row).

entries.name: continued_fraction_expansion
entries.description: Compute continued fraction expansion of a real number.
entries.reason: Takes a float input and a tolerance; inherently real-valued/transcendental territory.

entries.name: cf_to_rational
entries.description: Convert continued fraction to rational number.
entries.reason: Takes a variable-length List[int] argument, not a fixed small arg count.

entries.name: rational_to_cf
entries.description: Convert rational number to continued fraction.
entries.reason: Produces a variable-length term list, not a fixed-cost output.

entries.name: convergents_sequence
entries.description: Generate sequence of convergents for a continued fraction.
entries.reason: Both list-typed input and variable-length list output.

entries.name: best_rational_approximation
entries.description: Find best rational approximation to x with denominator ≤ max_denom.
entries.reason: Float input (target real number x).

entries.name: convergent_properties
entries.description: Analyze properties of continued fraction convergents.
entries.reason: List argument plus an optional float target.

entries.name: sqrt_cf_expansion
entries.description: Find continued fraction expansion of √n (periodic for non-perfect squares).
entries.reason: Produces a variable-length periodic-term list.

entries.name: periodic_continued_fractions
entries.description: Analyze periodic structure of quadratic irrational continued fractions.
entries.reason: Takes a variable-length List[int] of numbers to batch-analyze.

entries.name: cf_solve_pell
entries.description: Solve Pell's equation x² - ny² = 1 using continued fractions.
entries.reason: Pell-equation fundamental solutions grow unboundedly large even for modest n, exceeding a fixed u32 result.

entries.name: e_continued_fraction
entries.description: Generate continued fraction expansion of e (Euler's number).
entries.reason: Continued-fraction terms of the irrational constant e; float/transcendental by nature.

entries.name: golden_ratio_cf
entries.description: Generate continued fraction expansion of golden ratio φ.
entries.reason: Irrational mathematical constant (golden ratio), not an exact integer computation.

entries.name: pi_cf_algorithms
entries.description: Generate various continued fraction approximations to π.
entries.reason: Irrational mathematical constant (pi), float by nature.

entries.name: calendar_approximations
entries.description: Find calendar approximations using continued fractions.
entries.reason: Takes a float year_length input.

entries.name: cf_convergence_analysis
entries.description: Analyze convergence properties of continued fraction approximations.
entries.reason: Float input x, convergence analysis of a real number.

entries.name: digit_sum
entries.description: Calculate the sum of digits of a number in given base.
entries.reason: cell80's digit_sum already sums decimal digits; the base parameter is a generalization of an already-covered behavior.

entries.name: digital_root
entries.description: Calculate the digital root (single digit obtained by repeatedly summing digits).
entries.reason: Genuinely new iterated behavior (repeat digit-sum to a single digit); has an exact closed form (1+(n-1) mod 9 for base 10), bounded and distinct from digit_sum.

entries.name: digit_product
entries.description: Calculate the product of digits of a number.
entries.reason: cell80's digit_product already computes the decimal digit product; base parameter is an extension of covered behavior.

entries.name: persistent_digital_root
entries.description: Calculate persistent digital root (number of steps to reach single digit).
entries.reason: Distinct new metric (count of digit-sum iterations to reach a single digit), bounded and not covered by digit_sum.

entries.name: digit_reversal
entries.description: Reverse the digits of a number.
entries.reason: Exact match: cell80's digit_reverse already reverses the decimal digits of n.

entries.name: digit_sort
entries.description: Sort the digits of a number in ascending or descending order.
entries.reason: Distinct bounded operation (sort digits ascending/descending into a small fixed-size buffer, max 5 digits for u16), not covered.

entries.name: is_palindromic_number
entries.description: Check if a number is palindromic in given base.
entries.reason: New bounded predicate (digit-array mirror check) with no existing cell80 equivalent.

entries.name: palindromic_numbers
entries.description: Find all palindromic numbers up to a limit.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length list of all palindromes up to a limit.

entries.name: next_palindrome
entries.description: Find the next palindromic number greater than n.
entries.reason: Bounded incremental search (next palindrome after n) with small deterministic cycle cost, distinct from anything existing.

entries.name: is_harshad_number
entries.description: Check if a number is a Harshad (Niven) number (divisible by sum of its digits).
entries.reason: Harshad/Niven check is exactly "digit sum divides n", trivially composed from digit_sum + divides.

entries.name: harshad_numbers
entries.description: Find all Harshad numbers up to a limit.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length list of Harshad numbers up to a limit.

entries.name: number_to_base
entries.description: Convert a number to specified base representation.
entries.reason: Bounded exact conversion (u16 input needs at most 16 digits in binary), fits a small fixed-size digit-array output rather than a string.

entries.name: base_to_number
entries.description: Convert a base representation string to decimal number.
entries.reason: Takes an arbitrary string argument, which doesn't fit the dialect's fixed numeric/array parameter conventions.

entries.name: digit_count
entries.description: Count the number of digits in a number for given base.
entries.reason: cell80's num_digits already counts decimal digits; base parameter is an extension of covered behavior.

entries.name: digit_frequency
entries.description: Count frequency of each digit in a number.
entries.reason: Returns a Dict[int,int], a variable-size keyed structure rather than a fixed small output.

entries.name: is_repdigit
entries.description: Check if a number has all identical digits (repdigit).
entries.reason: New bounded predicate (all digits identical) via a small digit-extraction loop, not covered.

entries.name: is_automorphic_number
entries.description: Check if a number is automorphic (its square ends with the number itself).
entries.reason: Genuinely new bounded check (n^2 ends with n); would need square_wide + pow10 + mod chained (too many hops to call composable), so a dedicated small cell fits better.

entries.name: automorphic_numbers
entries.description: Find all automorphic numbers up to a limit.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length list of automorphic numbers up to a limit.

entries.name: solve_linear_diophantine
entries.description: Solve linear Diophantine equation ax + by = c for integer solutions.
entries.reason: Bounded exact 3-arg problem (particular solution to ax+by=c via extended Euclid), escalates when gcd doesn't divide c — fits the checked-cell pattern, not currently covered.

entries.name: count_solutions_diophantine
entries.description: Count integer solutions to ax + by = c within given bounds.
entries.reason: 7 arguments and an effectively unbounded search range (x_max-x_min, y_max-y_min are caller-controlled), a poor fit for a fixed-cost cell.

entries.name: parametric_solutions_diophantine
entries.description: Generate parametric solutions to linear Diophantine equation.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length List[List[int]] over a caller-controlled parameter range.

entries.name: solve_pell_equation
entries.description: Solve Pell's equation x² - ny² = 1 for fundamental solution.
entries.reason: Fundamental Pell solutions can be astronomically large even for small n, inherently unbounded-magnitude.

entries.name: pell_solutions_generator
entries.description: Generate multiple solutions to Pell's equation x² - ny² = 1.
entries.reason: Generates a variable-length list of Pell solutions, each potentially unbounded in magnitude.

entries.name: solve_negative_pell_equation
entries.description: Solve negative Pell's equation x² - ny² = -1.
entries.reason: Same unbounded-magnitude issue as the positive Pell equation; not always solvable and solutions can be huge.

entries.name: pythagorean_triples
entries.description: Find Pythagorean triples (x, y, z) where x² + y² = z².
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length List[List[int]] whose size grows with limit, unbounded output.

entries.name: sum_of_two_squares_all
entries.description: Represent integer as sum of two squares x² + y².
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length list of all representations as a sum of two squares.

entries.name: solve_quadratic_diophantine
entries.description: Solve general quadratic Diophantine equation ax² + bxy + cy² + dx + ey + f = 0.
entries.reason: List-typed coefficient/bounds arguments plus a brute-force search over bounds, and variable-length output.

entries.name: frobenius_number
entries.description: Calculate the Frobenius number for given denominations.
entries.reason: Takes an arbitrary-length list of denominations; general Frobenius number computation is also NP-hard for many denominations.

entries.name: postage_stamp_problem
entries.description: Solve the postage stamp problem (exact postage with given denominations).
entries.reason: Takes an arbitrary-length list of denominations, unbounded input.

entries.name: diophantine_analysis
entries.description: Analyze a Diophantine equation and provide general information.
entries.reason: A descriptive/textual lookup helper (string arg, informational Dict reply), not a real computational primitive worth building at either layer.

entries.name: gcd
entries.description: Calculate the Greatest Common Divisor (GCD) of two integers using Euclidean algorithm.
entries.reason: Exact match: cell80's gcd already computes the Euclidean GCD of two integers.

entries.name: lcm
entries.description: Calculate the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of two integers.
entries.reason: Exact match: cell80's lcm already computes the least common multiple of two values.

entries.name: divisors
entries.description: Find all positive divisors of a number in sorted order.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length sorted list of all divisors of n.

entries.name: is_divisible
entries.description: Check if the first number is divisible by the second number (remainder is zero).
entries.reason: is_divisible(a, b) ("is a divisible by b") is exactly divides(b, a) with arguments swapped (divides(a,b) means "does a divide b") — same cell, no new behaviour.

entries.name: is_even
entries.description: Check if a number is even (divisible by 2).
entries.reason: Exact match.

entries.name: is_odd
entries.description: Check if a number is odd (not divisible by 2).
entries.reason: Exact match.

entries.name: extended_gcd
entries.description: Extended Euclidean algorithm. Returns gcd(a,b) and coefficients x,y such that ax + by = gcd(a,b).
entries.reason: cell80's mod_inverse/crt_solve_pair only inline extended Euclid internally; a standalone cell returning gcd plus Bezout coefficients (sign-magnitude pair) is a genuine, distinct, bounded gap.

entries.name: divisor_count
entries.description: Count the number of positive divisors of a number (divisor function τ(n)).
entries.reason: Exact match: cell80's factor_count already counts positive divisors (the tau function).

entries.name: divisor_sum
entries.description: Calculate the sum of all positive divisors of a number (divisor function σ(n)).
entries.reason: Exact match: cell80's sum_divisors already computes sigma(n).

entries.name: egyptian_fraction_decomposition
entries.description: Decompose a fraction into Egyptian fractions using greedy algorithm.
entries.reason: Greedy Egyptian-fraction expansion can produce arbitrarily large denominators/term counts even for small inputs (e.g. 5/121), unbounded output not fixed-cost.

entries.name: fibonacci_greedy_egyptian
entries.description: Alternative greedy algorithm for Egyptian fractions (Fibonacci method).
entries.reason: Duplicate of egyptian_fraction_decomposition within catalogue — the greedy algorithm IS the Fibonacci-Sylvester method, same concept.

entries.name: binary_remainder_egyptian
entries.description: Binary remainder method for Egyptian fraction decomposition.
entries.reason: Duplicate of egyptian_fraction_decomposition within catalogue — an alternative decomposition method for the same unbounded-output concept.

entries.name: unit_fraction_sum
entries.description: Sum a list of unit fractions and return the result as a reduced fraction.
entries.reason: Takes an arbitrary-length list of denominators.

entries.name: is_unit_fraction
entries.description: Check if a fraction is a unit fraction (numerator = 1).
entries.reason: A unit fraction is simply one whose numerator equals 1; trivially composed from the existing eq cell.

entries.name: egyptian_fraction_lcm
entries.description: Find common denominators for Egyptian fraction operations.
entries.reason: Takes an arbitrary-length list of denominators (unbounded input), unlike cell80's fixed 2/3-arg lcm/lcm3.

entries.name: harmonic_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth harmonic number H_n = 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + ... + 1/n.
entries.reason: Returns a float (sum of reciprocals), not an exact integer/fraction.

entries.name: harmonic_number_fraction
entries.description: Calculate harmonic number using exact fractions (returns as fraction).
entries.reason: Exact-fraction accumulation of 1/1+...+1/n via internal frac_add-style reduction, escalating once the denominator exceeds u32 (around n~25-30) — fits the checked-cell pattern, not covered.

entries.name: harmonic_partial_sum
entries.description: Calculate partial sum of harmonic series with given terms.
entries.reason: Returns a float, not exact.

entries.name: harmonic_mean
entries.description: Calculate harmonic mean of a list of positive numbers.
entries.reason: Takes a list of floats and returns a float.

entries.name: sylvester_sequence
entries.description: Generate the first n terms of Sylvester's sequence.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length list, and values grow doubly-exponentially, overflowing u32 by the 6th term.

entries.name: sylvester_expansion_of_one
entries.description: Express 1 as sum of unit fractions using Sylvester's sequence.
entries.reason: Same doubly-exponential growth and variable-length list output as sylvester_sequence.

entries.name: egyptian_fraction_properties
entries.description: Analyze properties of an Egyptian fraction decomposition.
entries.reason: Takes an arbitrary-length list of denominators.

entries.name: is_optimal_egyptian_fraction
entries.description: Check if Egyptian fraction representation is optimal (shortest possible).
entries.reason: Takes a list-typed representation argument plus brute-force optimality search.

entries.name: two_unit_fraction_representations
entries.description: Find all ways to represent a small fraction as sum of two unit fractions.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length List[List[int]] of representations.

entries.name: is_proper_fraction
entries.description: Check if a fraction is proper (numerator < denominator).
entries.reason: Exact match: cell80's frac_is_proper already checks numerator < denominator.

entries.name: improper_to_egyptian
entries.description: Convert improper fraction to mixed number and Egyptian fraction for fractional part.
entries.reason: The mixed-number part is covered by frac_to_mixed, but the Egyptian-fraction remainder part is unbounded (same issue as egyptian_fraction_decomposition), making the whole function a poor cell fit.

entries.name: egyptian_expansion_lengths
entries.description: Calculate the length of Egyptian fraction expansion for fractions 1/n.
entries.reason: Returns a Dict[int,int] over a range up to max_n, variable-size output plus unbounded Egyptian-fraction growth.

entries.name: shortest_egyptian_fraction
entries.description: Find the shortest Egyptian fraction representation by brute force search.
entries.reason: Brute-force search returning a variable-length Optional[List[int]], potentially expensive and unbounded.

entries.name: farey_sequence
entries.description: Generate the Farey sequence F_n of order n.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length List[List[int]] whose size grows ~3n^2/pi^2, unbounded output.

entries.name: farey_sequence_length
entries.description: Calculate the length of Farey sequence F_n.
entries.reason: Bounded exact computation (1 + sum of euler_totient(k) for k=1..n via an internal loop), genuinely new and not covered.

entries.name: farey_neighbors
entries.description: Find the neighbors of a fraction in a Farey sequence.
entries.reason: Bounded deterministic search for Farey-sequence neighbors of a fraction, distinct and not covered.

entries.name: mediant
entries.description: Calculate the mediant of two fractions.
entries.reason: The mediant is just (p1+p2)/(q1+q2), trivially composed from two add_checked_u32 calls (numerator sum, denominator sum) — not a reduced frac_add.

entries.name: stern_brocot_tree
entries.description: Generate path through Stern-Brocot tree to reach target fraction.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length path (sequence of L/R moves) through the tree, unbounded output shape.

entries.name: farey_mediant_path
entries.description: Find path through Farey sequence using mediant operations.
entries.reason: 5 arguments and a variable-length path output.

entries.name: ford_circles
entries.description: Generate Ford circles for fractions in Farey sequence F_n.
entries.reason: Returns a Dict containing a list of circles for the whole Farey sequence F_n, unbounded like farey_sequence.

entries.name: ford_circle_properties
entries.description: Analyze properties of Ford circles including tangency relationships.
entries.reason: Same unbounded-collection issue as ford_circles.

entries.name: circle_tangency
entries.description: Check tangency relationship between two Ford circles.
entries.reason: Ford-circle tangency is exactly |p1*q2 - p2*q1| == 1, the same cross-multiplication idea frac_cmp already uses, composed from existing multiply/abs-diff/eq cells.

entries.name: farey_sequence_properties
entries.description: Analyze comprehensive properties of Farey sequence F_n.
entries.reason: Comprehensive/composite Dict of properties over an unbounded Farey sequence.

entries.name: density_analysis
entries.description: Analyze density of Farey sequences as n increases.
entries.reason: Exploratory analysis returning a Dict across a range of n, descriptive rather than a fixed-cost primitive.

entries.name: gap_analysis
entries.description: Analyze gaps between consecutive fractions in Farey sequence.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length list of gaps between consecutive Farey fractions.

entries.name: best_approximation_farey
entries.description: Find best rational approximation using Farey sequences.
entries.reason: Float input (target).

entries.name: farey_fraction_between
entries.description: Find a fraction between two given fractions using Farey sequence properties.
entries.reason: Duplicate of mediant within catalogue — finding a fraction between two Farey-adjacent fractions is the mediant operation.

entries.name: farey_sum
entries.description: Calculate Farey sum of two fractions with applications to modular arithmetic.
entries.reason: Duplicate of mediant within catalogue — the "Farey sum" of two fractions is defined as their mediant, same formula.

entries.name: calkin_wilf_tree
entries.description: Generate levels of Calkin-Wilf tree related to Farey sequences.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length structure across tree levels.

entries.name: riemann_hypothesis_connection
entries.description: Explore connections between Farey sequences and the Riemann Hypothesis.
entries.reason: Exploratory/descriptive research function, not a real computational primitive at either layer.

entries.name: polygonal_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth s-gonal (polygonal) number.
entries.reason: Generalized s-gonal number formula (2-arg, bounded, exact); cell80 only has triangular (the s=3 special case), a genuine gap for arbitrary s.

entries.name: is_polygonal_number
entries.description: Check if a number is an s-gonal number.
entries.reason: Inverse check for the generalized s-gonal formula (analogous to triangular_inverse_exact but parametrized by s), not covered.

entries.name: polygonal_sequence
entries.description: Generate the first n s-gonal numbers.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length list of the first n s-gonal numbers.

entries.name: centered_polygonal_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth centered s-gonal number.
entries.reason: Distinct generalized formula (s*n*(n-1)/2+1), bounded and exact, not covered by anything existing.

entries.name: centered_triangular_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth centered triangular number.
entries.reason: Duplicate of centered_polygonal_number within catalogue (the s=3 specialization).

entries.name: centered_square_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth centered square number.
entries.reason: Duplicate of centered_polygonal_number within catalogue (the s=4 specialization).

entries.name: centered_hexagonal_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth centered hexagonal number.
entries.reason: Duplicate of centered_polygonal_number within catalogue (the s=6 specialization).

entries.name: pronic_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth pronic number (oblong number).
entries.reason: Pronic(n) = n*(n+1), trivially composed from add_checked_u32 then mul_checked_u32 (equivalently 2*triangular(n)).

entries.name: is_pronic_number
entries.description: Check if a number is a pronic number.
entries.reason: Inverse-search predicate; feasible via isqrt(4n+1) parity check but chains enough operations (isqrt, arithmetic, compare) to warrant a dedicated small cell rather than a brittle multi-call composition.

entries.name: pronic_sequence
entries.description: Generate the first n pronic numbers.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length list of the first n pronic numbers.

entries.name: star_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth star number (6-pointed star).
entries.reason: Distinct closed-form figurate number (6n(n-1)+1), bounded and exact, not covered.

entries.name: hexagram_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth hexagram number (Star of David).
entries.reason: Duplicate of star_number within catalogue — the hexagram (Star of David) number is the same sequence as the 6-pointed star number.

entries.name: octahedral_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth octahedral number.
entries.reason: Obscure Platonic-solid figurate number with low real-world value compared to the more broadly useful square_pyramidal/tetrahedral shapes.

entries.name: dodecahedral_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth dodecahedral number.
entries.reason: Obscure Platonic-solid figurate number, purely recreational-math value.

entries.name: icosahedral_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth icosahedral number.
entries.reason: Obscure Platonic-solid figurate number, purely recreational-math value.

entries.name: triangular_pyramidal_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth triangular pyramidal number (tetrahedral).
entries.reason: Duplicate of tetrahedral_number within catalogue — description explicitly says "(tetrahedral)", same sequence.

entries.name: pentagonal_pyramidal_number
entries.description: Calculate the nth pentagonal pyramidal number.
entries.reason: Obscure figurate-number family member with low real-world value beyond square_pyramidal/tetrahedral, which already cover the common pyramidal-number use cases.

entries.name: gnomon_number
entries.description: Calculate gnomon numbers for s-gonal numbers.
entries.reason: Trivial linear formula ((s-2)*(n-1)+1) derived from the not-yet-existing polygonal_number difference; too minor/derivative to warrant its own cell.

entries.name: collatz_sequence
entries.description: Generate the Collatz sequence (3n+1 problem) starting from n until reaching 1.
entries.reason: Returns the full variable-length trajectory list; sequence length is famously unbounded/unpredictable in general.

entries.name: collatz_stopping_time
entries.description: Calculate the Collatz stopping time (number of steps to reach 1).
entries.reason: Returns just a step count (not the trajectory); for n within u16 range this is a bounded loop well within a cycle budget, fitting the checked/escalate cell pattern, not covered.

entries.name: collatz_max_value
entries.description: Find the maximum value reached in the Collatz sequence.
entries.reason: Bounded loop tracking the peak value reached; distinct scalar output, not covered.

entries.name: kaprekar_sequence
entries.description: Generate Kaprekar sequence for a number with given digit count.
entries.reason: Kaprekar's routine provably converges in <=7 steps for standard digit counts; best shaped as a step-cell (like counter_step/bresenham_step) rather than returning a raw list, but the underlying computation is genuinely bounded and new. CAVEAT: as named this returns the whole intermediate sequence (list output) — not cell-shaped. Build as kaprekar_stopping_time (steps to reach the Kaprekar constant) instead, mirroring collatz_stopping_time/collatz_max_value's already-correct bounded-scalar framing, not a literal sequence-generator cell.

entries.name: kaprekar_constant
entries.description: Get the Kaprekar constant for a given number of digits.
entries.reason: Small bounded lookup (the known Kaprekar constant per digit count, e.g. 6174 for 4 digits), not covered.

entries.name: is_happy_number
entries.description: Check if a number is a happy number.
entries.reason: Bounded loop (repeated sum-of-squared-digits, cycle-detect at 4) converging quickly for u16-range n, genuinely new predicate.

entries.name: happy_numbers
entries.description: Find all happy numbers up to a limit.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length list of happy numbers up to a limit.

entries.name: is_narcissistic_number
entries.description: Check if a number is narcissistic (equals sum of its digits raised to the power of digit count).
entries.reason: Bounded exact check (n == sum of its digits each raised to digit-count power), not trivially composable from existing cells, genuinely new.

entries.name: narcissistic_numbers
entries.description: Find all narcissistic numbers up to a limit.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length list of narcissistic numbers up to a limit.

entries.name: look_and_say_sequence
entries.description: Generate the look-and-say sequence starting from a number.
entries.reason: String input and a variable-length list of strings output, entirely outside the integer-cell dialect.

entries.name: recaman_sequence
entries.description: Generate the Recamán sequence up to n terms.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length list and requires tracking an unbounded "seen" set as n grows, not a fixed-cost computation.

entries.name: is_keith_number
entries.description: Check if a number is a Keith number and show the sequence.
entries.reason: Technically bounded but a very obscure recreational-math curiosity with essentially no real-world/word-problem value, and notably more complex than the other digit-recurrence predicates.

entries.name: keith_numbers
entries.description: Find all Keith numbers up to limit.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length list of Keith numbers up to a limit.

entries.name: digital_sum_sequence
entries.description: Generate sequence by repeatedly applying digital sum until single digit.
entries.reason: Returns the full variable-length trajectory of digit sums (persistent_digital_root's step-count is the bounded-output version of this same idea).

entries.name: digital_product_sequence
entries.description: Generate sequence by repeatedly applying digital product until single digit or zero.
entries.reason: Returns a variable-length trajectory list, the digit-product analogue of digital_sum_sequence.

entries.name: compute_pi_leibniz
entries.description: Compute pi using the Leibniz formula: π/4 = 1 - 1/3 + 1/5 - 1/7 + ...
entries.reason: Computes the irrational constant pi via an infinite series; float by nature.

entries.name: compute_pi_nilakantha
entries.description: Compute pi using the Nilakantha series: π = 3 + 4/(2×3×4) - 4/(4×5×6) + 4/(6×7×8) - ...
entries.reason: Alternative series for the irrational constant pi; float by nature.

entries.name: compute_pi_machin
entries.description: Compute pi using Machin's formula: π/4 = 4×arctan(1/5) - arctan(1/239)
entries.reason: Machin-style arctan series for pi; float/transcendental.

entries.name: compute_pi_chudnovsky
entries.description: Compute pi using Chudnovsky algorithm (extremely fast convergence).
entries.reason: High-precision series for pi; float/transcendental, arbitrary-precision territory.

entries.name: compute_e_series
entries.description: Compute e using the infinite series: e = 1 + 1/1! + 1/2! + 1/3! + ...
entries.reason: Computes the irrational constant e; float by nature.
