entries.reason: Cell80's manhattan cell already computes |dx|+|dy| between two grid points exactly.

entries.name: geom_line_intersection
entries.description: Find intersection point of two lines in 2D space
entries.reason: Cramer's-rule intersection of two infinite lines is an exact rational point (2x2-determinant numerator/denominator over the 8 input coords); no existing cell computes it but it fits the project's exact-fraction convention.

entries.name: geom_segment_intersection
entries.description: Find intersection point of two line segments in 2D space
entries.reason: Matches the project's own already-named gap 'segments_intersect_int': an exact-integer boolean predicate (orientation/cross-product sign tests) for whether two segments cross; the actual crossing point extends geom_line_intersection's exact-fraction approach with segment-bound checks.

entries.name: geom_circle_intersection
entries.description: Find intersection points of two circles
entries.reason: Circle-circle intersection points generally require the sqrt of a discriminant and are irrational, with unbounded case analysis (0/1/2/infinite intersections).

entries.name: geom_point_in_polygon
entries.description: Check if a point is inside a polygon using ray casting algorithm
entries.reason: Ray-casting over an arbitrary-length vertex list doesn't fit cell80's fixed-arity substrate; the bounded 4-arg rectangle case is already covered by point_in_rect.

entries.name: geom_polygon_area
entries.description: Calculate the area of a polygon using the Shoelace formula
entries.reason: Shoelace summation over an arbitrary-length vertex list is unbounded arity; the fixed-size triangle/quad cases are already covered by shoelace_area_x2 and shoelace_area_x2_quad.

entries.name: geom_circle_area
entries.description: Calculate the area of a circle
entries.reason: Area = pi*r^2 with r bounded; a fixed Q16.16 PI constant gives a boundable-truncation-error result, the same shape as the already-shipped q_mul/q_sqrt cells.

entries.name: geom_circle_circumference
entries.description: Calculate the circumference of a circle
entries.reason: Circumference = 2*pi*r is a single constant-multiply with boundable fixed-point truncation error.

entries.name: geom_triangle_area
entries.description: Calculate the area of a triangle given three vertices
entries.reason: shoelace_area_x2 already returns exactly twice this triangle's area as an exact integer, the project's convention for keeping a half-integer area representable exactly.

entries.name: vector_angle
entries.description: Calculate the angle between two vectors in radians
entries.reason: arccos of a normalized dot product over arbitrary-dimension vectors needs both an inverse-trig approximation and unbounded vector length.

entries.name: vectors_parallel
entries.description: Check if two vectors are parallel (or anti-parallel)
entries.reason: 2D case reduces to an exact cross-product-sign check (ax*by - ay*bx == 0), matching the project's own already-named 'orientation2d' gap, which doesn't exist yet; general N-dim plus float tolerance is out of scope.

entries.name: vectors_orthogonal
entries.description: Check if two vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular)
entries.reason: 2D exact orthogonality is exactly is_zero applied to dot2's output; the general N-dim plus float-tolerance version is out of scope.

entries.name: triple_scalar_product
entries.description: Calculate the triple scalar product of three 3D vectors
entries.reason: a.(bxc) for three 3D integer vectors is an exact bounded integer (a 3x3 determinant, sum of products/differences, no division or sqrt); 9 input fields is consistent with shoelace_area_x2_quad's 8-field precedent.

entries.name: triple_vector_product
entries.description: Calculate the triple vector product a×(b×c)
entries.reason: ax(bxc) expands via the BAC-CAB identity into pure integer dot-products and scalar multiplies (b*(a.c) - c*(a.b)); exact and bounded for 3D integer vectors.

entries.name: vector_norm
entries.description: Calculate the norm (magnitude) of a vector
entries.reason: Generic p-norm with arbitrary real p and arbitrary-dimension vectors needs pow()/root() with non-integer exponents.

entries.name: euclidean_norm
entries.description: Calculate the Euclidean norm (L2 norm) of a vector
entries.reason: 2D magnitude is exactly isqrt of the already-existing norm2_sq; general N-dim is unbounded arity and out of scope.

entries.name: manhattan_norm
entries.description: Calculate the Manhattan norm (L1 norm) of a vector
entries.reason: L1 norm from the origin is exactly Manhattan distance to (0,0), reusing the existing manhattan cell.

entries.name: chebyshev_norm
entries.description: Calculate the Chebyshev norm (L∞ norm) of a vector
entries.reason: L-infinity norm from the origin is exactly Chebyshev distance to (0,0), reusing the existing chebyshev cell.

entries.name: p_norm
entries.description: Calculate the p-norm of a vector for any p >= 1
entries.reason: Arbitrary real p (including fractional) requires a general power/root, and vector length is unbounded.

entries.name: normalize_vector
entries.description: Normalize a vector to unit length
entries.reason: Dividing by a generally-irrational L2 norm produces non-integer components; arbitrary-dimension input is also unbounded.

entries.name: dot_product
entries.description: Calculate the dot product of two vectors (inner product)
entries.reason: Cell80's dot2 computes exactly this for the practical 2D case; the general arbitrary-dimension version is unbounded arity, which cell80 doesn't attempt.

entries.name: cross_product
entries.description: Calculate the cross product of two 3D vectors
entries.reason: 3D cross product's three components (ay*bz-az*by, etc.) are exact bounded integer products/differences from 6 integer inputs; no sqrt or division needed.

entries.name: scalar_multiply
entries.description: Multiply a vector by a scalar value
entries.reason: 2D scalar scaling is just two saturating multiplies via the existing mul_sat cell; general N-dim is unbounded and out of scope.

entries.name: vector_add
entries.description: Add two vectors element-wise
entries.reason: 2D vector add is two saturating adds via the existing add_sat cell; general N-dim is unbounded and out of scope.

entries.name: vector_subtract
entries.description: Subtract one vector from another element-wise
entries.reason: 2D vector subtract composes from the existing sub_sat cell per component (note: sub_sat floors at 0, so true signed subtraction with negative components isn't fully captured); general N-dim is out of scope.

entries.name: element_wise_multiply
entries.description: Multiply two vectors element-wise (Hadamard product)
entries.reason: 2D Hadamard product is two saturating multiplies via the existing mul_sat cell; general N-dim is unbounded and out of scope.

entries.name: element_wise_divide
entries.description: Divide two vectors element-wise
entries.reason: 2D elementwise divide-by-zero safety is exactly what safe_div already provides, called per component; general N-dim is out of scope.

entries.name: vector_projection
entries.description: Project one vector onto another
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: frac_scale(dot2(a,b), norm2_sq(b), bx) and frac_scale(dot2(a,b), norm2_sq(b), by)
entries.reason: 2D projection of a onto b is (dot2(a,b)/norm2_sq(b))*b, an exact fraction per component obtainable by chaining dot2, norm2_sq and frac_scale, no new cell needed.

entries.name: vector_rejection
entries.description: Calculate vector rejection (component perpendicular to another vector)
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: frac_sub_from_whole(ax, dot2(a,b)*bx, norm2_sq(b)) per component, via the same dot2/norm2_sq/frac_scale chain as vector_projection
entries.reason: Rejection = a - projection(a,b); reuses vector_projection's exact-fraction composition plus frac_sub_from_whole, all existing cells.

entries.name: scalar_projection
entries.description: Calculate scalar projection of one vector onto another
entries.reason: Scalar projection = a.b/|b|; chaining dot2, norm2_sq, isqrt and q_div (whose (a<<8)/b signature matches directly) gives a Q8.8 result from existing cells alone.

entries.name: orthogonalize
entries.description: Orthogonalize a vector with respect to a set of vectors
entries.reason: Orthogonalizing against an arbitrary-size basis set is an unbounded iterative Gram-Schmidt-style reduction.

entries.name: gram_schmidt
entries.description: Apply Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization to a set of vectors
entries.reason: Full Gram-Schmidt over an arbitrary list of arbitrary-dimension vectors needs normalization (sqrt) and unbounded iteration.

entries.name: mean
entries.description: Calculate the arithmetic mean (average) of a list of numbers. Sum all values and divide by count.
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: mean3(a,b,c) for n=3; safe_div(accumulate_step(...).sum, count) for streaming arbitrary n
entries.reason: Fixed-arity mean already exists as mean3; an arbitrary-n streaming mean composes from the already-shipped accumulate_step + safe_div (the running-stats pack's own documented composition).

entries.name: median
entries.description: Calculate the median (middle value) of a list of numbers. The value that separates the higher half from the lower half.
entries.reason: median3 already covers the fixed 3-value case exactly; general arbitrary-n order statistics are unbounded and don't generalize via composition.

entries.name: mode
entries.description: Find the mode (most frequently occurring value) in a list of numbers. Returns all values that appear most frequently.
entries.reason: mode3 already covers the fixed 3-value case exactly; general arbitrary-n mode-finding is unbounded.

entries.name: variance
entries.description: Calculate the sample variance of a list of numbers. Measures how spread out the numbers are from the mean.
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: running_variance_step (per value) -> div_floor_u32(m2, count) [or count-1 for sample variance]
entries.reason: running_variance_step's own docs literally note composing with div_floor_u32 for the variance; population vs sample is just the caller's denominator choice.

entries.name: standard_deviation
entries.description: Calculate the standard deviation of a list of numbers. The square root of variance, showing typical deviation from mean.
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: isqrt(div_floor_u32(m2, count)) for integer stddev, or q_sqrt(...) for Q8.8 fractional precision
entries.reason: Chaining the existing running_variance_step/div_floor_u32 composition with the existing isqrt or q_sqrt cell gives stddev without any new cell.

entries.name: range_value
entries.description: Calculate the range (difference between maximum and minimum) of a list of numbers.
entries.cell80_id_or_composition: range3(a,b,c) for n=3; running_min_max_step for a streaming arbitrary-n range
entries.reason: Fixed-arity range already exists as range3; an arbitrary-n streaming range composes from the already-shipped running_min_max_step (returns max-min directly).

entries.name: comprehensive_stats
entries.description: Calculate comprehensive statistics for a dataset including mean, median, mode, variance, and more.
entries.reason: A convenience dict bundling mean/median/mode/variance/etc.; duplicates the other functions already listed separately in this same chunk rather than being a distinct primitive.

entries.name: percentile
entries.description: Calculate percentiles of a dataset. Find the value below which a certain percentage of data falls.
entries.reason: Arbitrary percentile of an arbitrary-length sorted dataset needs interpolation over unbounded data with no fixed-arity reduction.

entries.name: quartiles
entries.description: Calculate quartiles of a dataset (Q1, Q2/median, Q3). Divides data into four equal parts.
entries.reason: Special case of percentile (Q1/Q2/Q3) over an unbounded dataset; same sorting/interpolation requirement.

entries.name: covariance
entries.description: Calculate the covariance between two datasets (measures how variables change together)
entries.reason: A bivariate running-sums state cell (running sum_x, sum_y, sum_xy, count) mirroring running_variance_step's exact/checked pattern but for two variables; genuinely missing.

entries.name: correlation
entries.description: Calculate the Pearson correlation coefficient between two datasets (ranges from -1 to 1)
entries.reason: Pearson r is bounded to [-1,1] given precomputed sums (sum_x, sum_y, sum_xy, sum_x2, sum_y2, n) -- ideal for a Q8.8 cell using q_sqrt/q_div, though the general arbitrary-list aggregation must happen upstream.

entries.name: linear_regression
entries.description: Perform linear regression to fit y = mx + b and return slope, intercept, and R²
entries.reason: Given precomputed sums (sum_x, sum_y, sum_xy, sum_x2, n), the slope is an exact rational number obtainable via frac_reduce-style arithmetic, mirroring the project's frac_* exactness convention; general arbitrary-list aggregation and R^2 are out of scope for a single cell.

entries.name: moving_average
entries.description: Calculate moving average (rolling average) of a dataset
entries.reason: Produces a list output over an arbitrary-length input with an arbitrary window -- both unbounded; a fixed window of 3 trivially reduces to mean3 but the function's actual shape doesn't fit a bounded cell.

entries.name: z_scores
entries.description: Calculate z-scores for a dataset (standardized values)
entries.reason: zscore_q8 already computes exactly (value-mean)*256/stddev per element in Q8.8; z_scores just maps this over a list, whose mean/stddev come from composing the variance chain.

entries.name: detect_outliers
entries.description: Detect outliers in a dataset using z-score or IQR method
entries.reason: Per-element outlier flagging composes zscore_q8 with abs_i16 and is_gt; the batch scan over an unbounded list and the alternative IQR method are out of scope for a single cell.

entries.name: t_test_one_sample
entries.description: Perform one-sample t-test to test whether sample mean differs significantly from population mean
entries.reason: Needs the continuous Student-t CDF/p-value over arbitrary-length data; transcendental and unbounded.

entries.name: t_test_two_sample
entries.description: Perform two-sample t-test (independent samples) to test whether two sample means differ significantly
entries.reason: Same t-distribution p-value requirement as t_test_one_sample, over two arbitrary-length samples.

entries.name: paired_t_test
entries.description: Perform paired t-test (dependent samples) to test whether paired observations differ significantly
entries.reason: Same t-distribution p-value requirement, over paired arbitrary-length samples.

entries.name: z_test
entries.description: Perform z-test for known population standard deviation to test whether sample mean differs from population mean
entries.reason: The z-statistic itself is zscore_q8-shaped (mean vs population mean over a standard error), but the function's real value-add is the normal-CDF p-value, which is transcendental.

entries.name: chi_square_test
entries.description: Perform chi-square goodness-of-fit test to test whether observed frequencies match expected frequencies
entries.reason: Needs the continuous chi-square CDF over an arbitrary-length frequency list.

entries.name: confidence_interval_mean
entries.description: Calculate confidence interval for population mean from sample data
entries.reason: Needs a t-distribution critical value (depends on continuous df) plus arbitrary-length sample aggregation.

entries.name: confidence_interval_proportion
entries.description: Calculate confidence interval for population proportion from sample proportion
entries.reason: Needs an inverse-normal critical value for an arbitrary confidence level.

entries.name: cohens_d
entries.description: Calculate Cohen's d effect size for two samples (standardized difference between two means)
entries.reason: Cohen's d = (mean1-mean2)/pooled_std is exactly zscore_q8's formula reused with the two means and a precomputed pooled std; the pooled std itself comes from the existing variance-composition chain over each (unbounded) sample.

entries.name: effect_size_r
entries.description: Convert t-statistic to effect size r (correlation coefficient)
entries.reason: r = t/sqrt(t^2+df) from just two bounded scalar inputs (t_statistic, df); fits a small Q8.8 cell using the existing q_sqrt/q_div shapes.

entries.name: anova_one_way
entries.description: Perform one-way ANOVA (Analysis of Variance) to test whether means of multiple groups differ significantly
entries.reason: Arbitrary number of arbitrary-length groups plus an F-distribution p-value; unbounded on every axis.

entries.name: proportion_test
entries.description: Perform two-proportion z-test to test whether two population proportions differ significantly
entries.reason: Two-proportion z-test needs a normal-CDF p-value.

entries.name: sample_size_mean
entries.description: Calculate required sample size per group for comparing means (power analysis)
entries.reason: Power analysis needs inverse-normal critical values (z_alpha, z_beta) over continuous inputs.

entries.name: power_analysis
entries.description: Calculate statistical power (probability of detecting effect) for t-test given sample size and effect size
entries.reason: Same inverse-normal/continuous-distribution requirement as sample_size_mean.

entries.name: mann_whitney_u
entries.description: Perform Mann-Whitney U test (non-parametric alternative to t-test) to test whether two independent samples come from same distribution
entries.reason: Rank-based nonparametric test over two arbitrary-length samples plus a normal-approximation p-value.

entries.name: wilcoxon_signed_rank
entries.description: Perform Wilcoxon signed-rank test (non-parametric paired test) to test whether paired samples differ significantly
entries.reason: Same rank-based, unbounded-sample, continuous-p-value shape as mann_whitney_u.

entries.name: kruskal_wallis
entries.description: Perform Kruskal-Wallis test (non-parametric ANOVA) to test whether multiple independent samples come from same distribution
entries.reason: Rank-based nonparametric ANOVA over an arbitrary number of arbitrary-length groups plus a chi-square p-value.

entries.name: fishers_exact_test
entries.description: Perform Fisher's exact test for 2x2 contingency tables to test association between two categorical variables
entries.reason: The exact hypergeometric p-value for a 2x2 table is a ratio of three binomial coefficients, fully obtainable by chaining the existing choose_u32 and frac_reduce cells -- unlike the other inference tests, it has no continuous distribution to approximate.

entries.name: permutation_test
entries.description: Perform permutation test for difference in means (non-parametric test using random permutations)
entries.reason: Needs random resampling over arbitrary-length data with an arbitrary number of permutations; unbounded and stochastic.

entries.name: bootstrap_confidence_interval
entries.description: Calculate bootstrap confidence interval for a statistic (mean or median) using resampling
entries.reason: Needs random resampling (bootstrap) over arbitrary-length data; unbounded and stochastic.

entries.name: levenes_test
entries.description: Perform Levene's test for equality of variances to test whether groups have equal variances
entries.reason: Variance-equality test across an arbitrary number of arbitrary-length groups plus an F-distribution p-value.

entries.reason: C-to-F (F = C*9/5+32) is exact rational and would be composable, but C-to-K needs a non-integer offset (273.15) — the function bundles both under one multi-scale name, so the whole entry is host_only rather than splitting it into an exact and inexact half.

entries.cell80_id_or_composition: frac_of_whole(numerator, denominator, value) or mul_checked_u32(value, fixed_ratio)
entries.reason: Unit conversions are exact rational scalings — the spec's own Part 3 'Conversions: not authored — banked' call: owned by frac_of_whole/mul_checked_u32 compositions or the M2.5 unit base-scale table, not a new cell.
